about: Own-words reads from the daily research task (ADMIS, Rabobank, Czapp and the news feed). fund_score: -1 bearish to +1 bullish, a judgement on the fundamental news only.

corn.fundamental: Flat near 436 after new lows. Brazil's fast-growing corn-ethanol sector is absorbing more of its own corn and feeding a feedlot expansion, a slow-moving offset to Brazilian export competition; near term, fund selling still drives price.
events: Brazil's corn ethanol boom is speeding feedlot beef growth (Reuters)
Funds keep selling as corn and soybean export stories diverge (American Ag Network)
Ethanol groups push for ethanol in maritime fuel (Ethanol Producer Magazine)

soybeans.fundamental: Crush demand stays strong, but China is reportedly holding imported beans at ports as its domestic stocks swell, a soft signal for further US purchases ahead of the trade talks. Jan is up ~0.5% early on a crude bounce.
events: China holds soybean imports at ports as domestic supplies swell (Bloomberg)
Strong crush demand supports basis (Brownfield)
Mixed overnight finish for soybeans (Brownfield)

meal.fundamental: Meal gives back a little (-0.4%) as soyoil firms with crude; heavy crush keeps meal supply ample, so its relative strength depends on oil staying weak.
events: Soymeal the outlier on Wednesday (ADMIS)
Strong crush pace (Brownfield)

oil.fundamental: Soyoil firms ~0.75% with crude's Hormuz-driven rebound after Wednesday's slump; with crush running hard, supply is ample and the energy link remains the main driver.
events: Crude steadies as Hormuz tanker attacks offset glut fears (OilPrice.com)
Soyoil fell below support Wednesday (Barchart)

wheat.fundamental: A short-covering bounce (~+0.9%) after the lowest close since January; nothing new on supply, and Black Sea truce hopes plus improving El Niño moisture for US winter wheat keep the backdrop heavy.
events: Chicago wheat hit its lowest since January before bouncing (Investing.com, Brownfield)
El Niño seen improving the US winter wheat outlook (Brownfield)

kc.fundamental: HRW leads the bounce (~+1.9% in Mar); El Niño moisture for the Plains is still a supply positive for the 2027 crop, so this reads as short covering.
events: KC wheat rebounds overnight after breaking support (Yahoo Finance)
El Niño improving US winter wheat outlook (Brownfield)

cotton.fundamental: No new supply news; prices steadied after Wednesday's macro-driven slide. Dec is in delivery, so cert flow and the high-grade share matter more than the crop story for old-crop longs until Mar takes over.
events: Dec cotton fell with outside pressure Wednesday (Barchart)
Texas yield cut again in USDA's November report (RFD-TV)

hogs.fundamental: Feb fell ~2% Wednesday as the selloff to contract lows widened; Thailand access is a slow, small offset and nothing yet suggests cash is turning.
events: Lean hogs at new contract lows (ADMIS, Barchart)
Thailand deal includes US pork access (AgWeb)

cattle.fundamental: Tight supply backdrop unchanged and futures firmed while waiting on cash trade. Tyson's beef segment is still losing money on high cattle costs, a reminder of packer margin strain; USDA restricting European ruminant germplasm as Shamonda virus spreads is a precaution with no US herd impact so far.
events: Cattle futures mostly higher awaiting direct trade (Brownfield)
Tyson beats on earnings but beef remains a drag (Barron's)
USDA restricts ruminant germplasm from Europe as Shamonda virus spreads (Feedstuffs)

feeders.fundamental: Feeders firmed (~+0.9%) with the cash index near 338 and corn at lows supporting feeding margins; smaller December daily limits are coming.
events: CME to reduce feeder cattle daily limits in December (DTN)
Corn near new lows lowers feed costs (Successful Farming)

class3.fundamental: Block-led spot cheese weakness pushed Dec Class III down ~1% to about 17.1; a2 Milk's China-label recovery is a minor export-demand positive.
events: Dairy lower Wednesday, cheese blocks led losses (Brownfield)
a2 Milk's China-label offtake recovers (Reuters)

class4.fundamental: Spot dairy was lower across the board Wednesday; the Class IV nowcast still sits above futures on firm NDM.
events: Dairy prices lower Wednesday (Brownfield)

palm.fundamental: No new headlines for this market in the last 30 hours.
events: Jan ~4,272 (-29) (Bursa via TradingView)
Soyoil and crude lower (TradingView)

natgas.fundamental: Dec gives back ~1.5% after Wednesday's rally. Further attacks appear to be slowing LNG exports through Hormuz, which tightens the global LNG market and supports demand for US cargoes, while storage still ends the season slightly above normal.
events: LNG exports through Hormuz appear to slow after more attacks (Bloomberg)
Orlen in talks with QatarEnergy on a new LNG deal (Reuters)
US storage ended injection season above normal (EIA)

crude.fundamental: WTI rebounds ~1% to about 84 as fresh Hormuz tanker attacks offset the surplus story from this week's US stock builds; the market keeps trading between ample supply and Gulf shipping risk.
events: Oil steadies as Hormuz tanker threats offset glut fears (OilPrice.com, Reuters)
China's small refiners squeezed without Iranian crude (Reuters)
Explosion at an Indonesian refinery (Reuters)

ulsd.fundamental: Diesel slips ~0.8% even as crude firms; stocks remain well below normal with wide cracks, and Bapco's return to full capacity is a gradual bearish factor.
events: Distillate inventories built on the week but stay below normal (EIA)
Bapco refinery heading back to full capacity (Reuters)

rbob.fundamental: RBOB edges up with crude, but last week's large gasoline build and stocks above normal keep the seasonal-demand picture soft.
events: Gasoline stocks rose 5.2 mb, above the 5-year norm (EIA)
Crude rebounds on Hormuz attacks (OilPrice.com)
